item.title: Beginner Granny Squares - August — Sun Aug 23, 12:30 PM — Bistitchual
item.description: This listing is for a Beginner Granny Square Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Sunday August 23rd from 12:30pm - 2:30pm Bring your yarn over and pull through to our two hour granny square class! From blankets; to sweaters; to bags; and much more, these cozy squares can be used in a wide range of designs. They’re a joy to make, simple to reproduce and easy to customize to your own style and project needs. This class teaches how to make a basic granny square, how to change colours and, how to join squares together. We’ll discuss variations in construction and further possibilities. We expect students in this class to already know how to chain, make single and double crochets. You’ll need a 5.0 mm hook and worsted weight yarn in 2-3 colours. Materials are not provided, please bring your own or purchase these supplies at Bistitchual with a 10% discount, before class begins! Required materials: - worsted weight wool in a few different colours - 5.0mm hook Cancella

Get Tickets
Become a Member
This exhibition features the work of Magnus Hara, recipient of the 2024 Gardiner Museum Prize, awarded to a graduate of the Sheridan College Ceramics Program. Through alteration and combination of intimately known forms, this collection of vases is a reclamation of joy and autonomy after grief, loss, and injury. Intuitive assemblies of form, pattern, and configuration are used to question and confront the familiar in a dynamic visual language.

item.title: Festival Select: Smoke Signals (Chris Eyre, 1998) — Mon Sep 28, 6:00 PM — North York Central Library
item.description:
Join the Society and Recreation department of the North York Central Library for monthly screenings of fiction and non-fiction films that push the boundaries of the medium. This month we are showing Chris Eyre's Smoke Signals (1998). Synopsis (Criterion Pictures): Smoke Signals tells the story of the relationship between a father and his son. The story unfolds as Victor Joseph and another young man from the Indian reservation, Thomas Builds-the-Fire, set off to collect Arnold Joseph's pick-up truck and ashes from Arizona after Arnold has died. The two men remember Victor's father along the way, but their recollections are very different from each other. Victor learns many things about his father during his journey and, in the end, begins to understand, forgive, and grieve his loss. No registration required.

item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Sine Lam — Thu Oct 1, 12:00 AM — Forest Hill
item.description: Throughout the month of October, works by artist Sine Lam will be on display at the Forest Hill branch. Sine Lam is an emerging artist currently based in Ontario. She studied Fine Art at St. Lawrence College. Her artistic practice blends symbolism, realism, and surrealism, drawing inspiration from human emotion, urban solitude, connection, memories, nature, and time. Her series, Passage of Time , reflects her experiences of city life and explores themes of contrast and contradiction— visual beauty paired with melancholy, and relaxation alongside loneliness, much like life itself, where joy and sorrow coexist. Her work often carries hidden messages through symbolic elements. Sine's work has been featured in various group exhibitions, including at the Marianne van Silfhout Gallery. This exhibit is part of TPL's Art Exhibit Space program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city.
